stops.title: What this paper does
stops.text: DeepCache makes an image diffusion model faster without any retraining, by reusing work from one denoising step in the next. Up to now the atlas has made each network call cheaper with fewer bits. This paper asks a different question: why repeat a call that barely changes? Following it takes two things first, the U-Net and the sampling loop. Let's look at both.

stops.title: The U-Net and its skips
stops.text: Here is a U-Net. The left side goes down and shrinks the image into abstract features, the bottom is the deepest part, and the right side comes back up. The dashed teal lines are skip connections: they carry fresh, detailed information straight across. That shape is the whole trick. DeepCache keeps only the top, shallow blocks running and plugs in a stored copy of what arrives from below, at the indigo dot.

stops.title: Why reuse is possible
stops.text: Now the loop. Sampling calls the same U-Net at every timestep, often fifty or even two hundred and fifty times. Neighbouring steps see almost the same input, so their deep features are nearly identical. The bottom row shows the idea with an interval of three: one full step stores the deep feature, and the next two steps run only the cheap shallow path and reuse it.

stops.title: Words to hold on to
stops.text: A few terms before starting. The cache interval, called N, is how often the full network runs. The branch, called m, is how deep the cheap path goes. Quality is measured with FID, where lower is better, and CLIP score, where higher is better. And every speed number comes from one NVIDIA RTX 2080 card, so expect different timings on Intel.

stops.title: Where it sits
stops.text: Finally, the map. Quantization and FlashAttention-2 make a single call cheaper; DeepCache is the first paper that saves work across calls, so the two ideas can stack. Keep one caveat in mind: it relies on U-Net skips, and LTX-2.3 is a transformer without them. The next paper, TeaCache, fixes exactly that. Next comes the guided tour.
